Article Title: Amazon layoffs hit devices and ‌services unit; company's 'early morning' email to laid off employees says: A thorough review of ​our ...
Article Text:
Representative Image

Amazon unveils new lineup of Alexa devices

Amazon's open memo to engineers

Amazon layoffs are back. Ecommerce giant has announced new job cuts. According to a report in Reuters, Amazon is cutting about 250 jobs in its devices and ‌services unit after weeks of product rollouts including new Kindle e-readers and tablet computers. The company reportedly confirmed the job cuts after a Reuters inquiry. "We've made the difficult decision to eliminate a small number ⁠of roles," a spokesperson said. The layoffs will help the company "operate more efficiently and better align with our product roadmap," the statement added.According to the report, quoting a person familiar with the matter, the ​layoffs impact no more than 250 jobs, and are primarily in software development teams. As is the company's custom, text messages and emails were sent to employees early Wednesday morning (October 28). A layoff email, reportedly seen by ​Reuters, was ​from Cherie ⁠Robinson, a human resources vice president in devices and services, saying ​that the company had undergone "a thorough review of ​our ⁠structure" resulting in the need for cuts.In January this year, Amazon announced that it is cutting 16,000 jobs across the company.This announcement came after the e-commerce company laid off 14,000 people in October. During January layoffs, senior VP of People Experience and Technology Beth Galetti told employees that these layoffs were made for “reducing layers, increasing ownership, and removing bureaucracy.” She noted that the reason for the second round of massive layoffs within three months was that several teams in the company hadn’t finished their restructuring. “Some of you might ask if this is the beginning of a new rhythm – where we announce broad reductions every few months. That’s not our plan. But just as we always have, every team will continue to evaluate the ownership, speed, and capacity to invent for customers, and make adjustments as appropriate,” she said.Incidentally, the job cuts in the devices division came on the day Amazon unveiled five new Alexa-powered devices including a redesigned Echo Show 16 smart display and a photo frame with ‌built-in Alexa. The new product launches come as Amazon pushes its latest version of the voice assistant into customers' homes. Amazon is rolling out the devices as it ⁠faces growing competition from rivals including Apple, as well as AI companies such as OpenAI that have hardware ambitions.The Echo Show 16, which has a ​16-inch screen, built-in Fire TV and Amazon's ⁠first Echo Show camera with night vision, ​is priced at $499.99. A new Echo Studio ​speaker with a built-in camera, which lets Alexa recognize objects held up to it and lets users check ​on a room remotely, is priced at $249.99. The new Echo ​Dot is priced at $99.99. The device includes a built-in smart home hub and ‌Wi-Fi ⁠extender for the first time.Echo Time is a bedside clock, priced at $199. According to the company, it uses sleep-sensing technology to wake users during lighter sleep, without a wearable device. The Alexa ​Photo Frame, ​starting at $199.99, ⁠syncs pictures automatically from Amazon Photos.Just a day earlier, Amazon published a memo it shared with engineers in September on its website. Titled: 'Update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AI'; the memo has Amazon engineering leaders revise the role guideline for software development engineers, underscoring what matters most is the outcome, not which tools are used. "We all need to embrace this change and take the time to learn, or we risk being left behind. We’re just seeing the beginning of AI’s effect on software engineering. While we have a vision for what the future looks like, there’s a lot that’s still emerging. We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice," reads the memo.
Article Summary: Report: Amazon is cutting about 250 jobs in its devices and ‌services unit. The company reportedly confirmed the job cuts after a Reuters inquiry. In January this year, Amazon announced that it is cutting 16,000 jobs across the company. This announcement came after the e-commerce company laid off 14,000 people in October.

Article Title: Zomato’s new feature will hide menu prices when guests order food; Deepinder Goyal says…
Article Text:
User suggests a new way to make group ordering easier on Zomato

‘No price, no embarrassment, no hesitation’

Zomato CEO Deepinder Goyal responds

Food delivery platform Zomato is all set to roll out a new feature called ‘Mehmaan Mode’ which will hide the prices of food items while placing order, after a suggestion from a user on LinkedIn caught the attention of Zomato CEO Deepinder Goyal. The feature aims to make group food ordering more comfortable by allowing hosts to pass around their phones without guests seeing the cost of individual dishes or the overall order.The idea was proposed by LinkedIn user Ayushmaan Agarwalla, who shared a post suggesting that Zomato introduce a simple “Mehmaan Mode” for situations where friends, family members or guests are placing orders together. According to Agarwalla, it has become increasingly common for hosts to hand over their phones to guests so they can choose what they want to eat. However, the visibility of menu prices can sometimes create awkwardness, making people hesitant to order what they actually want.In his post, Agarwalla suggested a feature that would make prices disappear from the screen while guests browse menus and select dishes. Once the ordering is complete, the host could take the device back and proceed with payment. He argued that removing price visibility would allow guests to order more comfortably, without worrying about how expensive an item might appear to the person paying for the meal.Explaining the rationale behind the idea, Agarwalla wrote that a dedicated Mehmaan Mode would help eliminate the social discomfort that sometimes accompanies group ordering. “No price, no embarrassment and no hesitation,” he wrote, adding that the feature could be particularly useful during the festive season, when friends and extended families often gather and order meals together.The suggestion resonated with many users online as it addressed a common social situation in which guests may consciously avoid ordering certain items after noticing their prices, even when the host has encouraged them to choose freely.The proposal quickly received a response from Deepinder Goyal, who indicated that Zomato would move ahead with the feature. Replying to the LinkedIn post, the Zomato chief wrote, “Thanks for the suggestion. Shipping it this week. Wish you the happiest festive season ❤️.”
Article Summary: Zomato is set to roll out a new feature called ‘Mehmaan Mode’ which will hide the prices of food items while placing order. The feature aims to make group food ordering more comfortable by allowing hosts to pass around their phones without guests seeing the cost of individual dishes or the overall order.

Article Title: Pensioners, you can submit your life certificate from home: Who can apply, how it works and the November 30 deadline
Article Text:
Dates and deadline for 2026

What you need

How it works

Submission is not the same as acceptance

If you can’t use a smartphone

Pensioners in India do not have to queue at a bank or pension office to prove they are alive. They can generate a Digital Life Certificate (DLC) from home on a smartphone, using the government’s Jeevan Pramaan facility. The service lets pensioners submit their annual life certificate electronically, using Aadhaar-based face authentication without visiting a bank branch. The yearly certificate is what keeps pension payments from being interrupted.Presioners who are 80 years old and above can submit their life certificate from October 1 to November 30, 2026. On the other hand, those below 80 years if age canPensioners aged 80 and above can submit their life certificate from October 1 to November submit it from November 1 to November 30. With the November window about to open for most pensioners, anyone who has not yet submitted should plan to do it early and not leave it to the last weekFor face authentication, pensioners need an Android smartphone with an internet connection and a suitable front camera. They must download two apps, AadhaarFaceRD and the Jeevan Pramaan Face App. The sources I found describe the process only for Android phones, so iPhone users should check the official Jeevan Pramaan website for their options.The process is also tied to Aadhaar. As per the State Bank of India, the submission of life certificate is an Aadhaar-based process as it helps in the digital authentication and it works only if the account of the pensioner is seeded with their Aadhar number.Before starting the process, the pensioners should check whether their Aadhaar card is linked to their pension account and that the mobile number registered with Aadhaar is active, as the process also requires OTP.The steps vary slightly by app version, but the general flow is simple.1. Check your Aadhaar links. The digital life certificate can be authenticated only if your pension account is seeded with your Aadhaar number, and keep your Aadhaar-registered mobile number active for the OTP.2. Use a compatible phone. You need an Android smartphone with an internet connection and a suitable front camera.3. Download the two apps. Install AadhaarFaceRD and the Jeevan Pramaan Face App.4. Open the Jeevan Pramaan app and register. Enter your Aadhaar number and mobile number, then verify with the OTP.5. Fill in your pension details. These include pensioner type, PPO number, bank and disbursing agency.6. Complete face authentication. Capture your face with the phone’s front camera and follow the on-screen instructions.7. Save your Pramaan ID. A unique ID is generated once the process succeeds. You will also get an SMS with a transaction ID.8. Download your certificate. Use the transaction ID at jeevanpramaan.gov.in to download the computer-generated certificate for your records.9. Confirm it was accepted. A successful face scan doesn’t necessarily mean the pension authority has accepted the certificate, so check with your bank or disbursing agency before November 30.An important caution is that a successful face scan does not automatically mean the pension authority has accepted the certificate. Business Standard notes that pensioners should visit the Jeevan Pramaan portal after submission and use the Pramaan ID to access their certificate. Pensioners should also keep the ID and SMS, and check with their bank or disbursing agency that the certificate has been recorded before the deadline.Not everyone is comfortable with apps. SBI says a physical life certificate will continue to be accepted if the pensioner prefers it. Other routes include fingerprint or iris devices, the UMANG app, and help at banks, post offices and Common Service Centres. Government campaigns have also run special camps through pension disbursing banks and India Post Payments Bank, and traditional methods remain available for those who cannot access the digital platform. Family members and neighbours can help older pensioners with the smartphone process, but the pensioner must be present for the face scan
Article Summary: Pensioners in India do not have to queue at a bank or pension office to prove they are alive. They can generate a Digital Life Certificate (DLC) from home on a smartphone. The service lets pensioners submit their annual life certificate electronically. The yearly certificate is what keeps pension payments from being interrupted.

Article Title: Is Apple's new iPad mini becoming too expensive for its own audience?
Article Text:
Big upgrades, bigger price tag

Is Apple testing the loyalty of mini users?

Apple's smallest iPad has just received one of its biggest upgrades. It has also become considerably more expensive. At Rs 82,900, the new iPad mini raises an uncomfortable question: how much are consumers willing to pay for the convenience of a compact tablet?The latest model, announced on Monday, brings an OLED display, a powerful A20 Pro processor, improved connectivity and water resistance. On paper, it represents a substantial improvement over its predecessor. But the price changes the conversation.The previous iPad mini, launched in October 2024, started at Rs 49,900 in India. The new model costs Rs 33,000 more, representing an increase of about 66%. The Wi-Fi and cellular variant starts at Rs 1,00,900, taking Apple's smallest tablet past the psychological Rs 1 lakh mark. That’s just a lot of money for the iPad mini. Heck, it’s a lot of money for any iPad.For a product historically valued for its portability and relatively accessible entry point into the iPad ecosystem, that is a significant shift.Apple has a persuasive argument for the increase. The new 8.5-inch OLED screen promises richer colours, deeper blacks and better contrast than the LCD panel on the previous generation. Peak brightness reaches 1,200 nits, while thinner bezels allow Apple to increase screen size without substantially enlarging the device.The new mini is also thinner, measuring 5.4mm, and gains IP67-rated protection against water and dust.Inside, the A20 Pro chip delivers substantial performance improvements. Apple claims up to 60% faster multithreaded CPU performance, 2.7 times faster graphics and 4.5 times better AI performance compared with the previous generation.There is support for Wi-Fi 7, a landscape-oriented 12MP front camera, faster charging and Apple's latest intelligence features. These are meaningful improvements, particularly for users who intend to keep their tablets for several years.The iPad mini occupies an unusual position in Apple's portfolio. Its attraction is precisely what limits it: the small screen.For reading, note-taking, travelling, casual gaming and accessing documents on the move, the mini can be an excellent companion. It fits into spaces where larger tablets become cumbersome and offers considerably more working room than a smartphone.Doctors using digital records, pilots accessing flight information, field workers and artists sketching on the move may find the form factor particularly useful. But these are relatively specialised requirements.For someone primarily watching videos, attending online classes, browsing websites or working on documents, a larger iPad may offer a more comfortable experience. A MacBook, meanwhile, remains better suited to sustained typing, complex spreadsheets and multitasking.That creates a difficult proposition for the new mini. At Rs 82,900, buyers are being asked to pay a considerable premium for a screen that is deliberately smaller than those on many less expensive tablets.Apple Pencil Pro costs Rs 11,900, pushing the combined price to Rs 94,800. Adding the new Rs 8,500 Smart Folio takes the package to Rs 1,03,300.Even the more affordable USB-C Apple Pencil adds Rs 7,900.For students, occasional creators and consumers seeking a secondary device, that is a substantial investment in a tablet that cannot fully replace a laptop.Apple's pricing also reflects a broader change in its product strategy. Rather than positioning every smaller device as a more affordable alternative, the company increasingly treats compactness itself as a premium feature. Engineering a powerful processor, sophisticated display and advanced components into a smaller enclosure carries costs, but it also allows Apple to target customers willing to pay for a specific experience.This approach may work for the mini's loyal audience. Unlike larger tablets, where buyers can choose from numerous screen sizes and price points, the market for genuinely compact premium tablets remains limited. Apple therefore faces less direct competition for customers who specifically want a small, high-performance device.The 2024 iPad mini already offered strong performance, Apple Pencil support and access to Apple's extensive tablet app ecosystem. For many existing owners, the new display and processor may not dramatically change everyday tasks.There is also the question of artificial intelligence. Although Apple is emphasising the A20 Pro's capabilities, the usefulness of increasingly sophisticated on-device AI features will depend on how well they improve common activities, rather than merely how quickly the processor completes benchmark tests.Indian buyers are particularly sensitive to this distinction. Premium devices have an established audience, but a Rs 33,000 increase substantially narrows the pool of consumers who can justify an upgrade.Apple may be comfortable with that trade-off. The company does not necessarily need the mini to become a mass-market bestseller. A smaller group buying higher-priced devices could still support the product commercially.Whether that strategy strengthens the mini over time is another question.The new iPad mini is unquestionably more capable. Its OLED screen, lighter construction and improved processing power make it attractive for users who genuinely benefit from carrying a compact tablet.But for everyone else, the value proposition has weakened.At Rs 82,900, the iPad mini is no longer an easy recommendation as a convenient second screen. It is a specialised premium device whose size must be central to the buyer's needs. Apple has made its smallest iPad better than ever. The real question is whether it has also made it too expensive for many of the people who once loved it.
Article Summary: Apple's smallest iPad has just received one of its biggest upgrades. It has also become considerably more expensive. At Rs 82,900, the new iPad mini raises an uncomfortable question: how much are consumers willing to pay for the convenience of a compact tablet?

Article Title: Logitech launches limited-edition MX Master 4 Developer Edition mouse in India, priced at Rs 20,699
Article Text:
Availability and price

Logitech has expanded its premium peripherals portfolio in India with the launch of the MX Master 4 Developer Edition, a limited-edition version of its flagship productivity mouse designed specifically for software developers. The company said the special edition mouse combines the performance of the MX Master 4 with developer-inspired design elements, customisable controls and workflow features aimed at coding, AI-assisted development and multitasking.According to Logitech, the MX Master 4 Developer Edition has been created as a tribute to developers and the role they play in building digital products and services. The mouse features a distinctive design inspired by programming and software development culture, including laser-etched syntax symbols, markup tags, circuit traces and a "{Hello, World}" execution prompt across its matte-finish body. The device also includes several hidden references intended for developers. Among them are "0xFF + 1", a nod to World Programmers' Day, "09.17" referencing the Linux kernel release date and "!04.01" representing World Backup Day.Logitech said the design reflects the daily workflow of developers, from writing code and managing projects to debugging and working across multiple applications. The MX Master 4 Developer Edition builds on the feature set of Logitech's flagship MX Master 4 mouse.It includes customisable haptic feedback designed to assist with navigating large code repositories and switching between terminal windows.The mouse also features a dedicated Actions Ring button that provides one-click access to custom macros, shortcuts and AI coding assistants. Logitech says this can help developers streamline repetitive tasks and improve workflow efficiency.Another highlight is the company's MagSpeed Scroll Wheel, which can scroll through up to 1,000 lines per second while maintaining precise control for line-by-line navigation. Logitech describes it as its fastest, quietest and most accurate scrolling technology to date.The Logitech MX Master 4 Developer Edition is being offered as a limited-edition product and is now available through Amazon India while stocks last.
Article Summary: The MX Master 4 Developer Edition is a limited-edition version of Logitech's flagship productivity mouse. The mouse features a distinctive design inspired by programming and software development culture. It includes customisable haptic feedback designed to assist with navigating large code repositories and switching between terminal windows.

Article Title: A self-taught Birmingham teenager built a gesture-controlled robotic hand for about £30; the invention attracted 2.6 million views and requests from students worldwide
Article Text:
PC: HyphenOnline

How does Khan’s £30 gesture-controlled robotic hand work

Khan’s robotics projects attract followers on YouTube and TikTok

How did Khan build the Pepper humanoid robot at the age of 12

A self-taught teenager from Birmingham has attracted 2.6 million views on TikTok after building a gesture-controlled robotic hand for about £30. Suleymaan Khan, 17, developed the device using camera recognition and code he wrote himself, with materials including foamboard, card and hot glue. According to Hyphen, hundreds of people have contacted him to learn how to recreate the invention, while students around the world have sought his advice on robotics projects. Khan is now working on step-by-step kits to help others build the hand, alongside developing further robotic inventions.Khan's latest robotic hand is fully articulated and controlled through gestures. It uses camera recognition, supported by code that he wrote himself. The project demonstrates how he has progressed from simple homemade constructions to more complex robotic systems. Unlike his early cardboard creations, the hand combines physical components with programming to respond to recognised movements. The invention has attracted attention because Khan developed it using inexpensive, readily available materials rather than relying on costly specialist equipment.The cost of the project was approximately £30, according to Hyphen. Foamboard, card and hot glue were among the materials used to construct the hand. Its relatively low cost has prompted hundreds of people to ask Khan how to build a similar device themselves. He told the publication that he was working on putting together step-by-step kits to help people recreate the invention. The planned kits reflect the interest generated by the project and the requests he has received from people wanting to learn how the robotic hand works.Khan's robotics projects have developed a following on social media, where his work has reached audiences interested in technology and engineering. Hyphen reported that he had more than 400,000 likes and 20,000 followers across YouTube and TikTok. The robotic hand alone received 2.6 million views on TikTok. Alongside this online attention, students from different countries have approached him for help with their own robotics work, including university assignments and projects that they have struggled to complete.Khan described how students in Dubai contacted him shortly before his interview with Hyphen, seeking advice about a university assignment involving a robot. He has increasingly made helping other people an important part of his work. Reflecting on his development as an inventor, he said, “It’s cool to see where I started”. His experience illustrates how online platforms have enabled a young robotics enthusiast to share his projects with an international audience and connect with learners seeking practical technical guidance.Before developing the gesture-controlled hand, Khan built several other projects, including remote-controlled paper planes and a humanoid robot called Pepper. He created Pepper when he was 12, using LEGO Mindstorms, cardboard and dental floss. The robot could move around, pick up and carry objects in its arms, and use motion sensors in its eyes to help prevent collisions. Although Pepper is now damaged and can no longer stand independently, the project helped Khan learn how to build more complex machines while working with limited resources.Pepper also earned Khan the 2023 Network Rail national innovation award at the Big Bang Fair, a UK science and engineering competition for young people aged 11 to 18, according to Hyphen. He has since secured an apprenticeship at a local robotics company while continuing to develop his own creations in his spare time. His next project is another humanoid robot that he hopes will incorporate artificial intelligence for speech recognition, object recognition and home mapping. Khan has also expressed an interest in developing prosthetics in the future, identifying their cost as an area he would like to address through his work.
Article Summary: Suleymaan Khan, 17, from Birmingham, developed the device using foamboard, card and hot glue. It uses camera recognition and code he wrote himself. Khan is now working on step-by-step kits to help others build the hand, alongside developing further robotic inventions.

Article Title: Scientists analysed 640 charcoal fragments from a Spanish rock shelter and found Neanderthals may have organised different areas around ancient fireplaces
Article Text:
PC: AI Generated

Charcoal fragments reveal differences in Neanderthal activity around fireplaces

Wood fragments offer clues about Neanderthal fuel collection

Water-related changes affected charcoal remains across the shelter

What do the charcoal remains reveal about ancient activity at the shelter

Charcoal remains from a Spanish rock shelter are offering clues to how Neanderthals organised their living spaces. Researchers examined 640 charcoal fragments from level Ra at Abric Romaní, a site near Capellades in Barcelona. Their analysis found a concentration of charcoal around hearths in the northern sector, while the southern sector contained smaller and more isolated patches.According to research published in the Journal of Paleolithic Archaeology titled “ The Use of Space in Neanderthal Campsites: Evidence from Spatial and Taphonomic Analyses of Charcoal Remains from Level Ra of Abric Romaní (Barcelona, Spain) ”, the charcoal fragments were concentrated around hearths in the northern section, while the southern section contained smaller, more scattered accumulations.The researchers mapped charcoal fragments recovered during excavations from 2019 to 2022 and compared their locations with hearths and signs of natural alteration. The northern sector contained 495 fragments, many in broad concentrations overlapping with hearths near the shelter wall. The southern sector held 145 fragments in smaller, more isolated patches with less consistent overlap with hearths.The team used spatial analysis to examine whether these differences reflected human activity or later natural movement. After accounting for signs of water-related alteration, the distribution still suggested different uses of the two areas.Wood identification showed that mountain pine accounted for about 75% of the charcoal record. The researchers grouped several mountain pine species because their wood anatomy makes them difficult to distinguish. They noted that Neanderthals probably collected fuelwood from the area around the shelter, where pine was abundant.The charcoal’s condition was consistent with deadwood in varying states of decay, probably including many branches. Compression wood was common, a feature that can occur in branches as well as in trees growing under stress. The team said further analysis would be needed to distinguish branches from trunks more clearly.The charcoal had also been affected by natural processes after it was deposited. Researchers identified mineral concretions and other changes linked to water carrying dissolved minerals through the shelter. These alterations were proportionally more common among fragments from the southern sector, complicating the interpretation of its smaller charcoal patches, although the northern squares, near the wall, had higher absolute counts of altered fragments.The study found that water-related processes affected specific parts of the site, but overall post-depositional disturbance was low to moderate. The team considered human activity the main influence on the charcoal’s distribution, while acknowledging that natural processes could explain some patterns.According to the researchers, the southern charcoal patches may indicate discrete hearth-cleaning events, during which burned remains were moved a short distance away from fireplaces.They also considered whether the deposits formed during separate visits, with later groups reusing existing hearths. The charcoal alone cannot distinguish between these possibilities. The team recommended studying the distribution of stone tools, bones, and sediments alongside the hearths to build a picture of activity at the shelter. Such evidence could help establish whether charcoal was displaced in one occupation or accumulated across several.
Article Summary: Charcoal remains from a Spanish rock shelter offer clues to how Neanderthals organised their living spaces. Researchers examined 640 charcoal fragments from level Ra at Abric Romaní, a site near Capellades in Barcelona. Their analysis found a concentration of charcoal around hearths in the northern sector, while the southern sector contained smaller and more isolated patches.

Article Title: Oregon’s 1989 dam diverted water to one landowner’s pond; its 2020 removal kept his water right via a pump and reopened 1.8 miles of creek for coho salmon
Article Text:
AI-generated representative image of a small creek dam in a wooded area, illustrating a barrier that once disrupted natural stream flow and salmon migration. Image credits: ChatGPT

A dam that blocked fish passage for three decades

a

Removing the barrier and restoring the channel

Coho salmon in a river. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Beyond the former barrier, coho salmon were detected

A dam built across Kelley Creek in 1989 in Oregon blocked migrating fish from reaching upstream habitat for three decades while diverting water into a private owner’s pond. The structure was nearly six feet tall, and it reportedly obstructed fish passage through the lower part of the creek, a tributary within the Johnson Creek watershed near Portland. In August 2020, the Johnson Creek Watershed Council (JCWC) removed the dam and substituted its gravity-fed water diversion with a pump, thus allowing the landowner to continue using his water right. 1.8 miles of accessible habitat as the project’s target was identified by the Clackamas Partnership. This was intended to be an opening route that would benefit coho salmon, steelhead and Pacific lamprey. Subsequent environmental DNA observation detected coho salmon at the former dam site, thus providing evidence of their presence extending beyond the barrier.The dam was built at river mile 0.5 on Kelley Creek with the intention of holding water upstream and feeding a gravity-powered diversion into an off-channel pond. While the structure served the estateowner’s water needs, the structure spanned the creek and prevented fish like salmon, steelhead and lamprey from migrating into upstream habitat. The Clackamas Partnership classified this as a complete barrier to salmonid passage.Kelley Creek and its tributaries include habitat used by migratory fish, which made the obstruction a priority for restoration efforts in the wider Johnson Creek watershed.In 2015, the planning for fish-passage improvements began. Following this, in 2017, JCWC secured funding from the East Multnomah Soil and Water Conservation District, allowing consultants to explore options for bettering the passage. A 60% engineering design was reportedly completed in November 2018. The team initially considered ways to construct a route that fish could use to bypass the structure. However, when presented with the alternatives, the landowner reportedly suggested removing the dam altogether. That proposal moved the project towards eliminating the barrier while preserving the pond’s water supply.Meanwhile, engineers designed a submersible pump station downstream of the former barrier, near the pond, to replace the gravity-fed diversion. The Clackamas Partnership reported that the Oregon Water Resources Departmentpproved a formal amendment to the water right’s point of diversion and waived the associated processing fee. This pump provided the means of physically drawing water. Therefore, the dam could be removed without requiring the landowner to abandon the existing water use.In August 2020, the removal of the dam was finished. Prior to the demolition, teams slowly lowered the impounded water, exposing mudflats and giving Pacific lamprey buried in the sediment an opportunity to emerge so they could be captured and relocated. This gradual drawdown was aimed at reducing harm to aquatic life during construction. Following the dam’s removal, engineers installed an engineered streambed in the former structure’s footprint to reduce the risk of the channel eroding downwards or cutting sideways into its banks.The replacement water-diversion system also required some changes to the stream channel. Engineers built a riffle downstream to help maintain the pool needed for the pump intake. A screened intake was installed to lessen the risk of fish being drawn into the diversion, while a boulder weir helped direct the flow towards the centre of the pool and keep the screen clear of debris. These features allowed water withdrawal to continue without recreating the original barrier to fish migration.Furthermore, the restoration work included measures to protect the creek beyond the former dam site. According to JCWC, a fence along the stream to prevent livestock from entering the channel was installed alongside plans for riparian revegetation. The department believed that keeping livestock away from the creek can help protect streambanks and newly planted vegetation from trampling. Together, the channel reconstruction and streamside protection measures were intended to improve the stability of the restored reach and support its use by aquatic species.The project’s targeted performance measure listed 1.8 miles of accessible stream habitat along Kelley Creek. Its fact sheet identifies coho salmon, steelhead and Pacific lamprey as focal species. In a separate JCWC project documentation in 2020, it was reported that fish passage had been restored to a cumulative total of nearly three miles of Kelley and Mitchell creeks.Subsequent monitoring showed that coho salmon were present at the former dam site. The council’s environmental DNA programme, which analyses genetic material collected from stream water, reported coho salmon DNA at the site where the dam had been removed. The council later noted that coho detections at the site had continued across its sampling efforts.
Article Summary: A dam built across Kelley Creek in 1989 in Oregon blocked migrating fish from reaching upstream habitat for three decades. The structure was nearly six feet tall, and it reportedly obstructed fish passage through the lower part of the creek. In August 2020, the Johnson Creek Watershed Council removed the dam and substituted its gravity-fed water diversion with a pump. Subsequent environmental DNA observation detected coho salmon at the former dam site.

Article Title: A Texas artist began drawing portraits on rice using food colouring; her fleeting creations attracted millions of viewers and helped her build a million-subscriber channel
Article Text:
Alissa Teo has built Fried Rice Art into a business with nearly 4 million TikTok followers and more than 2 million YouTube subscribers. She creates rice portraits and tosses into the air to film them in her backyard. Image Credit: Fried Rice Art/Flower Mound Times

Rice portraits helped a Texas artist attracting millions of viewers

The painstaking process behind each fleeting creation

A social media following that grew into a business

How does the artist put leftover rice to use

An artistic idea built around making people smile

A Texas artist has transformed an everyday kitchen staple into a strange form of portraiture. She creates intricate images from colored rice which last only a fraction of a second. Fried Rice Art artist Alissa Teo arranges individual grains into recognizable faces and designs before throwing them into the air and shooting the moment on camera. Her work has reached millions of viewers on the web and turned a tiny creative experiment into a successful business. What began as a family activity in 2021 has since grown into a popular social media channel and a source of commercial commissions.According to KERA News, the Flower Mound artist developed her distinctive technique after spending more time at home with her family. Her background as a registered occupational therapist also influenced the idea, as rice had previously been a useful material for sensory activities with children.Teo began colouring rice and playing with it alongside her children during a period when her middle child was experiencing health complications. The activity offered a simple way for the family to spend time together while giving her an opportunity to return to her interest in art.As explained on the official Fried Rice Art website, Teo had enjoyed making art since childhood and had sold her work to classmates as a young artist. She later became an occupational therapist before changing her working arrangements to accommodate her family's needs.The rice creations eventually developed into something more ambitious. Her sister encouraged Teo to put her artwork on TikTok and she began posting her experiments online.Her early videos were garnering millions of views in days, the response much more than she had anticipated.Despite their playful appearance, Teo's portraits require considerable preparation and precision. A report by Flower Mound Times described how she creates the images in a corner of her backyard, using a mobile phone and a tripod to record the final toss.Before the camera starts rolling, she carefully arranges coloured grains of rice to form a recognisable image. Tweezers and rulers help her place the tiny pieces and a tracing of the intended design helps with placement of the different colors.Her work table is covered with many bottles of colored dye so that she can build portraits with different shades and fine details. The process demands patience because even a small mistake can affect the appearance of the finished image.When Teo’s done arranging the rice he tosses it in the air. The grains briefly take on the desired image and then disperse and fall apart.The camera takes that instant of change so that the spectator can see the construction and the deconstruction of the work at the same time.The appeal lies in the brief existence of each portrait. Teo does not paint a finished image on canvas or paper, but rather an image that is to exist for an instant.The video recording is the permanent record of the artwork and allows viewers to see a process they may never otherwise see.The popularity of Fried Rice Art has helped Teo establish a substantial online presence. According to her official website, she has attracted more than 3.5 million followers on TikTok and 2.1 million subscribers on YouTube.Her audience has opened opportunities beyond social media views. The official Fried Rice Art portfolio lists collaborations with well-known companies and entertainment brands, including Disney, LEGO, Crayola, ESPN, Paramount, Puma and the Houston Texans.These projects have allowed Teo to apply her unusual technique to commercial campaigns and familiar characters. Flower Mound Times reported that she created an image of Tow Mater from the Disney film Cars as part of a project connected with the film's world.The commissions demonstrate how an unconventional artistic idea can find an audience beyond its original setting. Instead of relying on traditional materials, Teo uses coloured rice to create images that work particularly well in short videos, where viewers can see the arrangement, the toss and the moment of transformation.Although the final toss scatters the carefully arranged grains, the rice does not necessarily go to waste. Teo's official website includes a dedicated section explaining how she reuses the material to make sensory bins for children.According to the website's sensory-bin guide, she catches much of the rice on a board beneath the artwork before collecting it and placing it in containers. She then adds age-appropriate toys and tools, such as tweezers, scoops, spoons and cups, to create activities for children.The containers can be adapted around different themes, including glow-in-the-dark designs. The tools also offer opportunities for children to practise coordination and fine motor skills by picking up, moving and sorting objects.This aspect of the business connects directly with Teo's earlier occupational therapy career. The same material that helps her create portraits for an online audience can also support hands-on activities for children.Teo's work has continued to cover a wide range of subjects, from recognisable characters and sports-related designs to flags, food, holidays and special occasions. Her official website says she has created more than 500 rice toss-ups for fans and companies combined.The variety allows her to respond to different audiences. Fried Rice Art describes the motivation behind the work as creating encouraging pieces that put a smile on people's faces. That approach also helps explain why the videos appeal to viewers who may have little interest in traditional art.
Article Summary: Alissa Teo has built Fried Rice Art into a business with nearly 4 million TikTok followers and more than 2 million YouTube subscribers. She creates rice portraits and tosses into the air to film them in her backyard. Teo does not paint a finished image on canvas or paper, but rather an image that is to exist for an instant.

Article Title: Meet homeless man Anders Fernstedt, who has lived outside London’s £210 million mansion for 3.5 years; how he survives without money, sleeps through winters and why neighbours let him stay
Article Text:
Anders Fernstedt has lived outside a £210 million mansion in London’s Knightsbridge for three and a half years. (Photo: DW Euromaxx)

How Anders Fernstedt ended up homeless

How he built a home outside a £210 million mansion

The 45-room mansion at Rutland Gate reportedly sold for £210 million in 2020 but remains unoccupied. (Photo: DW Euromaxx)

Why the neighbours let him stay

Anders Fernstedt relies on donated food, clothes and charitable services to meet his everyday needs. (Photo: DW Euromaxx)

How he manages without money, electricity or basic amenities

The homeless man uses portable power banks to keep his phone running and download books. (Photo: DW Euromaxx)

Why he says he finally feels at home

Anders Fernstedt says friendly conversations and small gestures from neighbours have helped him feel more secure. (Photo: DW Euromaxx)

A homeless man has been living outside one of London’s most expensive mansions for three and a half years, building an unusual home in one of the British capital’s wealthiest neighbourhoods. While the sprawling 45-room property remains empty, Anders Fernstedt has created a life for himself outside it, relying on donated food, clothes, books and a makeshift shelter.Located in Knightsbridge, the mansion at 2 to 8A Rutland Gate reportedly sold for £210 million in 2020. The property boasts views of Hyde Park, marble bathrooms, 116 windows and an indoor swimming pool. However, the buyer never moved in, leaving the luxurious property unoccupied for years.Fernstedt’s unusual living arrangement was explored in a video feature by DW Euromaxx, which followed him to understand how he ended up living outside the luxury property, how he manages without money and why some neighbours have accepted his presence.Fernstedt was raised by his mother in Sweden and later pursued several careers in Sweden and the United States, establishing himself in the technology sector. He moved to England in 2016 and worked as a journalist and fact-checker before work dried up around the Covid-19 pandemic.A share in a technology company from his time in the US provided him with savings that he relied on for several years. However, as freelance commissions became harder to secure, his money gradually ran out.“There was enough money for me to live off for a few years, but only frugally, half the time in a tent,” he explained.Fernstedt said he slowly became accustomed to living on less, to the point that he did not immediately realise when he had effectively run out of money.“I slowly got used to frugality that I didn't even notice when I stopped having money,” he said.Fernstedt initially thought the spot outside the mansion would provide shelter for a night. Instead, it became his home for years.An avid camper with an interest in nature, he has adapted his outdoor space to suit his needs. He compares his makeshift shelter to a Mongolian yurt or other traditional tents, describing the imaginative way he has created a home on the mansion’s porch.He has also accumulated belongings that help him feel secure and comfortable. Comparing his collection to a squirrel storing nuts, Fernstedt explained that having several supplies means he does not immediately notice when something goes missing.His sleeping arrangements are particularly important to him. He has built up a collection of duvets and bedding, including what he described as seven layers of Hungarian down.“I haven't had a bad night's sleep for as long as I can remember,” he said, adding that his arrangements help him sleep through all four seasons.Fernstedt has learned to adapt to outdoor living, including London’s winters. He explained that sleeping without walls can also allow air to circulate during warmer weather.Living outside a mansion in one of London’s most exclusive neighbourhoods might appear difficult, but Fernstedt says he has gradually developed relationships with people in the surrounding community.After spending a few weeks at the location, he realised that residents knew he was there. He began thinking about how to make his presence familiar without intruding on their lives.He said he believed the neighbourhood’s children and grandchildren could help make his case to their families, hoping that conversations at home would encourage residents to accept him.Over time, some neighbours began approaching him to ask whether he needed anything. Their gestures have included food, clothes and even an elegant Italian dinner jacket.Fernstedt said that beyond material donations, he values ordinary human interaction and friendly conversations with the people living nearby.Not everyone in the neighbourhood has welcomed his presence, but he has found support from residents who appreciate his efforts to keep his makeshift home tidy and his lifestyle quiet. Some reportedly believe his presence may also help deter thieves or vandals from targeting the empty property.The feature does not establish that Fernstedt has formal permission or a legal right to remain outside the mansion.Fernstedt describes himself as being almost completely disconnected from money. His daily expenses are minimal, with filter coffee among the few things he says he pays for.For essentials such as showers, food and clothing, he relies partly on charitable support. He visits a charity near Victoria that provides showers, a canteen and access to donated clothing and other basic necessities.The support helps him obtain everyday items, including socks, while occasional gifts from neighbours offer additional assistance.Without a conventional electricity supply, Fernstedt relies on several portable power banks to keep his devices running. He uses his phone to download books, including history titles and the diaries of filmmaker Andrei Tarkovsky.His collection of books and personal belongings offers a sense of continuity in a life that otherwise operates far removed from conventional housing and employment.Fernstedt’s current arrangement has given him a sense of security that he says he did not always experience in temporary accommodation.After living at the location for years, he no longer constantly worries that his belongings will disappear while he is away.“Because I've been here so long, I'm free of worrying now, and if we worry too much, we won't be happy,” he said.
Article Summary: Anders Fernstedt has lived outside a £210 million mansion for three and a half years. He relies on donated food, clothes, books and a makeshift shelter. The 45-room mansion at Rutland Gate reportedly sold for £210m in 2020. The buyer never moved in, leaving the luxurious property unoccupied for years.

Article Title: Stanford professors Sebastian Thrun and Peter Norvig opened their artificial intelligence course to the world for free in 2011; 160,000 students from 190 countries enrolled
Article Text:
Representative AI image of an artificial intelligence lecture and online learning setup. (Image Credits: ChatGPT)

A university course with assignments, tests, and international participation

Representative image of an individual viewing an artificial intelligence code screen. (Image Credits: Pexels)

International participation and the implications for higher education

In October 2011, professors from Stanford University made their introduction to Artificial Intelligence as a free course and open to anyone with internet access. Taught jointly by Stanford research professor Sebastian Thrun and Google research director Peter Norvig, who expected few sign-ups, the course exceeded their expectations when 160,000 enrolments came from more than 190 countries. According to Stanford Engineering , the course started on 10 October and ran until 18 December, forming part of a wider experiment that involved three online computer science courses offered by the university. Along with the artificial intelligence course, students enrolled in Introduction to Databases, which was taught by Jennifer Widom, and Machine Learning under Andrew Ng.Unlike a typical online setting where students can learn through online lectures, the classes were structured like a course of study. According to Stanford Engineering , the course was designed to offer students more than the scope of university lectures, wherein they could work through recorded mini-lectures, complete exercises, and take examinationsIntended to run for ten weeks, the syllabus covered the tenets of artificial intelligence through models of robotics, autonomous vehicles, and software that recommends music. Students were able to go through each week’s lessons at their own pace because the teaching materials were released weekly, while mid-term and final examinations were automatically assessed. To make the video lectures more interactive, quizzes were incorporated into the system. For students wanting to test their practical skills, programming exercises were in place to assess their knowledge. However, it would be remiss not to mention that those who completed the course requirements were awarded a statement of accomplishment, but participation did not confer Stanford University academic credit.Moreover, the design of the assessments was made in a way that allowed for repeated attempts. The one responsible for this interface was Stanford computer science professor emeritus, Jeffrey Ullman. Ullman had conceptualised a testing method that relied on a pool of possible answers rather than just the visible options on a single question. As a result, the system generated different question sets for each iterative attempt a student made on a given assessment.Furthermore, the system allowed an online discussion forum, much like the setting of a classroom where the floor is opened for questions. There, students could pose questions, answer the lingering doubts of their colleagues, and vote answers up or down based on their satisfaction. Jennifer Widom, who taught the databases course, reported that this was instrumental for teachers since they couldn’t cater to all the students at once; she said, "I can see that students are answering each other's questions and that answers from the top students are going to bubble up. "The impact of this artificial intelligence course was felt beyond the figures it had registered; Stanford Engineering reported that students had accessed the course database more than 7,500 times per second. About 40% of the total registrants across the three courses were from the United States, and India accounted for the second-largest group.Participation wasn't just limited to the formal teaching platform, as volunteers lent a helping hand and translated the artificial intelligence course into more than 40 languages, while local study groups were formed in different places to discuss the material in person. For instructors and teachers alike, the experiment provided an opportunity to understand how students learn and thereby improve their teaching methods. With tens of thousands of participants exposed to different testing arrangements, this exercise would have been otherwise difficult to conduct with a conventional class of 50 or 60 students.Ultimately, the course’s significance lies in establishing artificial intelligence as a barrier breaker and strengthening the groundwork of teaching methodology. Up until this initiative, institutions would publish lecture recordings for remote audiences. The Stanford experiment showed the possibility of combining video instruction with structured coursework and assessment on a much larger scale.
Article Summary: Stanford University offered an online course on artificial intelligence to 160,000 students from 190 countries. The course was designed to offer students more than the scope of university lectures. Students could work through recorded mini-lectures, complete exercises, and take examinations. Volunteers translated the course into more than 40 languages.

Article Title: In 2007, a Georgia fatherbegan turningthe tiny villages he made with his eight children into a stone garden of more than 50 miniature castles and cathedrals, now drawing visitors
Article Text:
Representative AI image of a miniature stone village featuring handcrafted castles, cottages and cathedrals set within a garden. (Image Credits: ChatGPT)

Materials and construction behind the miniature buildings

Image of the Colesseum in the Rock Garden near Calhoun. (Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons)

A community-maintained attraction

There is a miniature world of buildings and places from around the world in a garden behind a church in Calhoun, Georgia. Nestled beside a stream, the garden, also known as “The Rock Garden”, sits just behind the Calhoun Seventh-day Adventist Church on Rome Road. The garden boasts an array of miniature structures that resemble their larger counterparts, and these include several replicas of Paris’s Notre-Dame Cathedral, Japan’s Himeji Castle, and Rome’s Colosseum.The project was set off in 2007, when DeWitt Boyd, a church member known as “Old Dog”, started constructing the garden on the grounds of the church itself. According to Atlas Obscura, Boyd had created these villages as a game for his eight children, giving each child a porcelain figure to represent them in the imaginary settlements, until it eventually emerged as a collection of more than 50 miniature structures.Through hits and misses, Boyd created his method of utilising cement reinforced with a long list of materials, including wire, pebbles, shells, broken glass, and ceramic tiles to make the structures. According to a Blue Ridge Country feature on the garden and its builder, the building process demanded both time and strenuous manual effort. It took over 27 months to complete the Notre Dame Cathedral decked with stained glass windows.As per a Roadtrippers report, the garden’s construction methods were passed to volunteers who helped maintain the site. One such volunteer was Brandy Long, who worked with Boyd placing stones into cement to build foundations for larger features, including pillars and bridges.The garden is also rife with a mix of secular and biblical imagery; one of its miniature settlements includes Bethlehem, while the other consists of small-sized churches, a monastery, and cathedrals. Between these small villages and structures are narrow paths made of cobblestone for people to walk on, coupled with a gazebo and various seating areas. Christian allusions also appear in inscriptions and features on walls and paths; for instance, the Ten Commandments are represented by tablets embedded in a walkway. Besides the architectural models, there are miniature porcelain figures of people and animals; towering above it all is a real-life music pavilion, apt for accommodating performances.Beyond the aesthetic appeal, the garden served a wider purpose. According to the Calhoun Seventh-day Adventist Church’s official history of the Rock Garden, the ground serves as a place for reflection, prayer, and engagement with nature. The property also includes landscaped grounds and a one-mile dirt and gravel trail crossing two creek bridges.Boyd’s wife, Joyce Maples, also works in the garden, primarily looking after the Memory Wall, which has clay hearts to commemorate the marriages that took place in the Garden. The Roadtrippers reported a plaque commemorating Boyd and his wife, Joyce, who had also participated in the project. The same report highlights how the community remains involved in the garden, with volunteers learning construction techniques and undertaking repairs to preserve the structures. The garden’s development has therefore involved adding new features in tandem with maintaining existing ones, as exposed stonework and bridges require attention over time.For the community, the garden stands as a vibrant gathering hub and keeps its tradition alive by hosting an annual lighting ceremony in October. During the event, volunteers illuminate the miniature buildings and pathways with candles and lanterns. After daylight hours, the site is lit up by a display in which the windows, bridges, and individual structures become visible through their lighting.
Article Summary: The Rock Garden in Calhoun, Georgia, is a collection of more than 50 miniature structures. These include replicas of Paris's Notre-Dame Cathedral, Japan's Himeji Castle, and Rome's Colosseum. The garden was created in 2007 by DeWitt Boyd, a church member known as ‘Old Dog’

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:
Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile (Photo: AP).

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.

Article Title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
Article Text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a criticalseverity warning. (Reuters photo)

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities

BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems.Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual.
