Article Title: Chinese parents sue OpenAI over their daughter's death; say ChatGPT-maker could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits
Article Text:
Chinese parents sue OpenAI over their daughter's death; say ChatGPT-maker could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits

Lawsuit alleges ChatGPT advised her to reduce medication

Parents claim ChatGPT failed to recognise warning signs

Family calls for stricter limits on medical advice

What OpenAI says

Parents of a 31-year-old Chinese woman who worked as a software engineer at Amazon have reportedly sued OpenAI , alleging that ChatGPT encouraged their daughter to reduce her epilepsy medication without medical supervision before her death in February. The lawsuit claims the company could have prevented her death by making medical advice off-limits to its chatbot. According to a report by The New York Times, the lawsuit was filed by Qun Wan and Meiqin Xu over the death of their daughter, Bowen Wan. The complaint alleges that ChatGPT helped her plan a gradual reduction in her seizure medication and advised her not to tell her doctors about it.The case involves GPT-4o, an older version of ChatGPT that OpenAI removed from the service on February 13, a day after Wan died, according to the report. OpenAI described the case as “incredibly heartbreaking” and said newer models are better at recognising situations that require urgent attention.Bowen Wan had epilepsy and was taking lamotrigine, a medication that had reduced her seizures to a few episodes a month. In January 2026, she reportedly asked ChatGPT about lowering her daily dose because she feared the medication was affecting her speech and could hurt her chances in job interviews.The lawsuit alleges that the chatbot created schedules to reduce her dose to zero within weeks. It also claims that ChatGPT encouraged her to keep the plan from her doctors and supported her decision not to take a blood test that could have measured her medication levels.The report said Wan had also raised concerns about her medication in connection with her green-card application. According to the lawsuit, ChatGPT discussed how a lower dose might affect the medical examination required for the application.Dr. Nicholas Poolos, Wan’s neurologist, told The New York Times that he would not have recommended stopping the medication given her medical history.“No, not rational, no way,” he said. “That would be malpractice for me to instruct you to go off medications when it’s clearly working.”The lawsuit against OpenAI alleges that Wan continued to report symptoms, including confusion, memory gaps and unusual sensations, while reducing her medication. ChatGPT reportedly reassured her that these experiences were part of her brain adjusting to the changes.The New York Times said it reviewed more than 270,000 messages between Wan and ChatGPT. According to the report, she expressed concern about reducing her medication at least 158 times.In her final message to the chatbot on February 11, according to the complaint, Wan asked whether the pain in her head was similar to pain caused by a fever. The chatbot reportedly described the pain as “not dangerous” and said it was part of the recovery process.Her parents, who were in China, asked acquaintances to check on her. They found her body three days later. A postmortem test found a lamotrigine level of 0.64 micrograms per millilitre, about one-fifth of the lower end of the drug’s therapeutic range, the report said.Bowen Wan’s parents argue that OpenAI could have helped prevent her death by making medical advice a restricted category that the chatbot cannot provide, rather than allowing users to override the guidance.They point to OpenAI’s Model Spec, which sets out how its AI models should behave. The lawsuit argues that medical advice about prescription medication should have stronger restrictions, similar to the company’s firm rules in other areas.The case adds to a series of lawsuits alleging that ChatGPT encouraged users to rely on the chatbot instead of seeking support from people around them. In a separate case filed in 2025, the parents of a 16-year-old boy alleged that OpenAI prioritised user engagement over safety.OpenAI said the case involved an older version of ChatGPT and that newer models are better at identifying situations that require urgent attention. The company described the case as “incredibly heartbreaking”.Wan began using ChatGPT in 2023 for relationship advice and help with insurance and disability benefits. By 2025, she was reportedly sending more than 1,500 messages a week to the chatbot and speaking less frequently with her parents.Her parents told The New York Times that the messages were difficult to reconcile with the daughter they knew.“She’s not usually like this,” Xu said. “It’s like she was under a spell.”
Article Summary: Bowen Wan had epilepsy and was taking lamotrigine, a medication that had reduced her seizures to a few episodes a month. In January 2026, she reportedly asked ChatGPT about lowering her daily dose because she feared the medication was affecting her speech and could hurt her chances in job interviews. The lawsuit alleges that the chatbot created schedules to reduce her dose to zero within weeks and encouraged her to keep the plan from her doctors.

Article Title: Google just announced Genie 4: Here’s what it can do, from building walk-through worlds out of a sentence to filling them with sound and speech, and when you might get to try it
Article Text:
Google’s Genie 4 builds worlds you can walk through

Genie 4 builds a scene around you while you explore it

People, physics and sound now feel much closer to real life

Genie 4 is coming to paying subscribers first, and it still has rough edges

Type a line describing a quiet lake on a misty morning, with a man playing the saxophone on a small floating platform, and Google 's new AI will build that place for you. You can then move around it, glide the camera over the water and hear the saxophone as you go.This is Genie 4, the newest version of what Google calls a world model, unveiled by its research lab Google DeepMind on Tuesday. It is not open to the public yet, but a waitlist is already up, and the demos give a good sense of what it can do.Using it feels closer to playing a video game than watching a video. You start by typing a description or uploading a photo, and Genie 4 creates the scene on screen. Press the arrow keys to walk forward, turn around or move the camera, and it draws whatever lies in that direction, frame by frame, as you go.Unlike a game, nothing here was designed beforehand. There are no ready-made levels or characters waiting to be found, and everything you see is created the moment you look at it.You can also change the scene while you are in it. Type that you want it to start raining, ask for a different view or bring a new person into the frame, and the world adjusts without starting over. Behind the scenes, Google's Gemini AI makes sure these changes fit in naturally and that the place stays consistent as you move around.Each session can now run for around two minutes while staying consistent, roughly twice as long as the previous version, Genie 3.The biggest change from Genie 3 is how real everything looks. Objects move the way you would expect them to, so a falling maple seed spins on its way to the ground and things collide more convincingly.People are where you notice it most. Characters in the older version often moved stiffly, while those in Genie 4 walk naturally, react to what is around them and can be directed as the scene plays out. One of Google's examples is a crowded Japanese railway station from the 1980s, with passengers filling the platform and a long red train on the nearest track.Sound is new as well. Every scene now comes with its own audio, from waves on a beach to wind in the trees, and characters can speak. They chat with each other and respond to what you do or to whatever happens around them.A small group of testers has been putting all of this to use. Filmmakers are walking through scenes before shooting them, trying out camera angles, lighting and dialogue. Photographers are turning old photos into places you can step into, and game makers are testing ideas in minutes before writing a line of code. Google is also using it to let robots practise tasks in a simulated room before trying them in a real one.For now, only a small group of testers can use Genie 4. Google says it will reach AI Ultra subscribers in the coming weeks through Project Genie, its app for creating these worlds, along with developers who build apps on Google's AI. Ultra is the most expensive of Google's AI plans, and there is no word yet on whether the cheaper ones will get access later. Anyone interested can sign up for the waitlist on the Project Genie page.It is also clearly unfinished, and Google says as much. The longer you spend in a world, the more its details can drift, with objects changing shape or disappearing altogether. Sound does not always line up with what is on screen, and text such as signs or labels can come out hard to read.To keep its creations from being mistaken for real footage, every video and audio clip Genie 4 makes carries an invisible watermark that marks it as AI-generated.Typing a sentence and stepping into the place it describes is, at the moment, something only a handful of testers get to do, two minutes at a time. Google's plan is to widen that circle soon, starting with the people already paying for its top AI plan.
Article Summary: Genie 4 is coming to paying subscribers first, and it still has rough edges. Unlike a game, nothing here was designed beforehand. There are no ready-made levels or characters waiting to be found. Everything you see is created the moment you look at it.

Article Title: Roblox accused of scraping 145GB of 3D files for AI training, adult content included; 3D modelling site says: As far as our logs show, nobody…
Article Text:
(Image via: Roblox)

Update: This story has been updated with a statement from

Roblox

.

Original story follows

What happened

What Roblox has to say

Kids gaming platform Roblox has been accused of scrapping 145GB of 3D files for training artificial intelligence (AI). Independent 3D modeling community Open3DLab shared a blog post where it alleged that a crawler that “belonged to Roblox walked through almost every project on Open3DLab, SFMLab and SmutBase, and proceeded to download complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects. 145.5 GB of our creators' work, downloaded for what we assume are AI training purposes”. The crawler used trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com) as its user agent, with the data coming from a single Amazon AWS address.“We want to be careful here. We don't think Roblox set out to collect adult content, and we have no evidence that any of it reached a model or a product. The scrapes were likely automated. But that is exactly the problem: as far as our logs show, nobody checked. A crawler working for a company whose platform tens of millions of children use was pointed at an adult site, and it took explicit models without telling them apart from anything else,” the blog post reads.On Sunday, 18th of October, Open3DLab says it noticed a crawler making a large number of requests to sites and download infrastructure. The crawler sent the same user agent on every request, trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com).It came from a single Amazon Web Services (AWS) address. It had read the main page of 18,926 projects, which is practically the 3D modeling community’s entire catalogue, in 26,429 requests over a span of 34 hours.After pulling the project pages, it downloaded complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects, 145.5 GB in all, before suspending operations during the weekend. The downloads include 364 files (54.8 GB) from 224 projects on SmutBase, which hosts adult content only. With the SFMLab projects marked adult, 345 of the 712 projects (62.6 GB) are adult content.The main limiting factor in the number of files downloaded was the crawler's reliance on the free download servers, which have caps on speed limit and number of concurrent downloads. The crawler did not respect robots.txt, (which it did retrieve), ignored Terms of Service, (which forbid scraping), and defied the creators' licenses: 423 of the 712 projects are licensed for non-commercial use only. Within the sample it retrieved, it took adult projects at the same rate as everything else. Some examples include models of Eve from Stellar Blade, Mei from Overwatch, and a Horse cock dildo.The 3D lab says that after detecting the crawler on October 18, it “blocked further attempts the same morning”.Roblox reached out to TOI Tech with a statement.“A Roblox researcher built an agent to collect publicly available 3D assets that mistakenly scraped content from Open3DLab, failing to operate as intended. The agent was decommissioned and the data was not used for any purpose, including training any AI models. We are strengthening safeguards for how agents like this are built and reviewed, and will continue to do so as the agentic landscape evolves,” Roblox spokesperson told TOI Tech.
Article Summary: Roblox accused of scraping 145GB of 3D files for training artificial intelligence (AI) Independent 3D modeling community Open3DLab shared a blog post where it alleged that a crawler that ‘belonged to Roblox’ downloaded 1,027 files from 712 projects’ The downloads include 364 files from 224 projects on SmutBase, which hosts adult content only.

Article Title: Reddit now has two homepage feeds: What the new ‘For You’ and ‘Following’ tabs show you
Article Text:
Reddit splits its home feed in two

Reddit has been steering its homepage towards algorithms all year

Reddit is changing what users see the moment they open the app. The platform has split its homepage into two feeds, “For You” and “Following,” a format TikTok made popular, and the new layout is rolling out globally over the next few weeks.Following sticks to posts from subreddits a user has already joined. For You mixes those posts with recommendations based on their interests, including communities they browse but have never subscribed to. Someone who keeps checking r/Silksong without joining it could now find those threads near the top of their home feed.Reddit says the idea is discovery. In a blog post, the company described the new feeds as “a first step in helping drive discovery that leads to something novel and relevant.”Switching between the two takes a tap, and Reddit remembers the last one used. Close the app on Following, and it opens on Following next time.The shift has been building for months. Earlier this year, Reddit announced it would deprecate r/all, the page that surfaced popular posts from across the platform, as part of a push to simplify the site and personalise Home. Recommended posts from outside a user’s subreddits aren’t new either.They simply get their own dedicated space now.The change puts Reddit in line with Instagram, X, Threads and Facebook, all of which lean on “For You”-style feeds. Not every user is on board, though. Some who saw the feature during testing have already complained, and plenty of regulars value Reddit precisely because their feed reflects communities they picked.For them, Old Reddit at old.reddit.com still offers the classic “best,” “hot,” “new,” “rising” and “controversial” sorting. Reddit has said it will limit Old Reddit access for accounts that haven’t used it recently, blaming AI bots, so anyone attached to it should log in soon.
Article Summary: Reddit is changing what users see the moment they open the app. The platform has split its homepage into two feeds, “For You” and “Following” The new layout is rolling out globally over the next few weeks.

Article Title: Starting December, Discord will make some public server messages available on Google Search; here’s who’s included and how to opt out
Article Text:
Which servers and messages are included

Who is included by default

How can members opt out

What can server administrators control

Discord will soon make some public server messages searchable online. In a recent announcement, the company said messages from participating public channels in Discoverable Servers could appear on server web pages and in web search from mid-December 2026. The rollout will be gradual, so the first messages may take several weeks to appear.The change is intended to make community knowledge, including gaming guides and answers to common questions, accessible outside Discord. Administrators can decide which channels participate, while members can control whether their messages appear. The announcement refers to web search generally and does not specifically name Google Search. Private servers, direct messages and group direct messages are excluded.The changes apply only to Discoverable Servers, which include communities listed in Discord’s Server Discovery that anyone can join without an invitation. These servers must have at least 1,000 members, be at least eight weeks old, and meet activity and safety requirements.Only messages sent from mid-December onwards in participating public channels will be eligible.Earlier messages will not be included, regardless of a member’s settings. Discord will label channels whose content may appear on the web.Usernames and avatars will not appear alongside messages on Server Web Pages. Teen users are excluded from the Channel Messages feature and cannot enable it until adulthood.In the EU, UK, Canada, Brazil, Australia, and South Korea, the member setting is off by default. Members in these regions must enable it before their messages can appear.Elsewhere, the setting is on by default unless members turn it off. A message can appear only if the server’s administrators also allow the channel to participate.Members can disable sharing through these steps:1. Open User Settings2. Select Data and Privacy.3. Turn off “Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages”.The switch applies across every Discoverable Server the member belongs to. Discord began rolling out these controls on October 27, ahead of the message-sharing launch.Turning the setting off later prevents future messages from appearing. Messages shared while it was enabled remain online unless the member deletes them from Discord.Administrators can open Server Settings > Web Presence to select participating channels or exclude all channels. Public channels remain enabled by default if administrators make no changes.Every Discoverable Server will have a Server Web Page from November 16. If administrators have not created one, Discord will publish a default page using the server’s profile details.Automated Channel Summaries may also begin appearing that day, drawing on conversations from November 16 onwards. These summaries are controlled separately: a member opting out of message sharing does not disable them. Administrators can choose their source channels, curate the summaries, or turn them off entirely.
Article Summary: Discord will soon make some public server messages searchable online. Messages from participating public channels in Discoverable Servers could appear on server web pages and in web search from mid-December 2026. The rollout will be gradual, so the first messages may take several weeks to appear. Administrators can decide which channels participate, while members can control whether their messages appear.

Article Title: Meta AI director Rohit Patel leaves company after eight years; plans startup to take on Microsoft Office and Google Workspace; says adding AI to spreadsheets ‘kills my…’
Article Text:
In pic: Meta's ex-AI director Rohit Patel

What does Ndoc do

Why did Rohit Patel left Meta

When will Ndoc be available

Meta AI director Rohit Patel is leaving the company after eight years. According to a TechCrunch report, the former director at Meta Superintelligence Labs has launched Ndoc, a startup he is positioning as an AI alternative to Microsoft Office and Google Workspace. He aims to bring analysis, presentations, and underlying data into one workspace, eliminating the need to switch between separate apps.“Companies are basically attaching AI to spreadsheets and it fills your cells for you,” Patel told TechCrunch. “It just sort of kills my soul. This is like if you just figured out electricity, and then you decided the best use case is to put lights on my bulls that till my soil. No. Get a tractor.”Ndoc organises work into three connected tabs. Stage displays presentations, dashboards, simulations and small applications. Narrative contains written analysis, citations and generated figures. Model holds the underlying datasets and Python scripts, allowing users to inspect how results were produced.Users can upload data and ask the platform to analyse it and explain the findings. They can also provide context about the intended audience and tone.According to Patel, colleagues can access the shared workspace even without signing up for Ndoc.The emphasis on checking AI output reflects Patel’s work at Meta, where he focused on reinforcement learning, training AI through rewards and trial and error, and evaluating whether its output could be trusted.“Even if you don’t know any Python, you can ask [the AI chat] to explain, ‘Hey, what does this script do? Which line has my formula?’ And you can verify that formula,” Patel said. “There’s nothing hidden behind the curtain here.”Patel said his wish to make Ndoc’s document format openly available was partly behind his decision to leave. He believed securing agreement on such a format within Meta would involve input from many people and slow development.Ndoc can export documents as a single “.ndoc.html” file that opens in a browser, according to Patel. He plans to open-source the format so other developers can build compatible applications and users can access their work without depending entirely on Ndoc.The platform uses a mixture of open-source AI models. Patel claims this makes it considerably cheaper to operate than alternatives using more advanced proprietary models.Ndoc has a three-person team and has not raised funding, the report added. Patel said he wanted evidence of customer demand before approaching investors.The startup is running an enterprise pilot and offering an early test version to a limited number of customers via a waiting list. Signing up is free, but customers will pay for usage and tokens, the units AI models use to process information.Patel hopes to release a broader beta version in the coming weeks, with a full launch planned for next year. The company has also built connections to existing workplace tools so customers can import their data.
Article Summary: Rohit Patel is leaving Meta Superintelligence Labs after eight years. He has launched Ndoc, an AI alternative to Microsoft Office and Google Workspace. Ndoc organises work into three connected tabs. Stage displays presentations, dashboards, simulations and small applications. Narrative contains written analysis, citations and generated figures. Model holds underlying datasets and Python scripts.

Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

Article Title: Why smart TV owners are using AI to make their televisions 'dumb', and the risks that come with it
Article Text:
Claude Code is being used to make smart TVs ‘dumb’ again (Disclaimer: This is an AI generated image)

Ads, tracking and slow menus are pushing owners to 'dumb down' their TVs

Bricked sets and skipped security updates are the biggest risks

Ads on the home screen, menus that lag and software that quietly logs what you watch have pushed a growing number of smart TV owners towards an unusual fix. They are using AI coding agents like Claude Code to strip their Android TV and Google TV sets back to the apps and HDMI inputs they paid for, and the idea has spread fast across X and GitHub over the past week.The appeal is easy to see, but the method isn't risk-free. Some users have bricked their sets, others have got stuck halfway, and security experts warn that cutting a connected TV off from updates could open the door to bigger problems.Most modern smart TVs use automatic content recognition (ACR), which identifies what's playing through screenshots or audio clips. Manufacturers use that data to serve targeted ads and share it with ad partners. Opt-outs exist, but they are usually buried deep in the settings.Developer Gathin T. hit his limit with the ads on his parents' TV. He had Claude Code clean it up over Wi-Fi, build a home screen with just their apps, and shared the prompt online as cleanyourtv. Within two days, thousands had repeated it on Xiaomi, TCL, Sony and Fire TV sets, and the project now claims testing on over 80 models.Another project, dumbtv by Muzzammil Yasin Sabuwala, targets ads, telemetry, Alexa and ACR, and has been tested on Sony, TCL, Philips, Hisense and Xiaomi TVs.Both work through Android Debug Bridge (ADB), a developer feature built into Android-based TVs, so nothing is rooted and changes can be reversed.Speed is part of the draw too. One X user said an afternoon with Claude Code disabled 25 bloat apps and replaced a 192MB stock launcher with an 83MB custom one.In India, where Google TV powers a large share of sets from Xiaomi, TCL, Sony and several budget brands, the pool of potential tinkerers is big.Results vary widely. One user said Claude bricked their Android TV, another got stuck midway through a Fire TV attempt, and an attempt on a Samsung set ended with a bricked TV too. Samsung's Tizen, LG's webOS, Roku and Amazon's newer Vega-based Fire TV Sticks are largely out of reach, and tampering can void the warranty on a new set.Toronto-based cybersecurity expert Ritesh Kotak warns that blocking services and skipping updates on a TV that stays online could leave it exposed to hackers, particularly as many sets now carry microphones. Vibe-coded scripts are also rarely built with security first, and may not be maintained for long.Safer routes exist. Turning off ACR and personalised ads in settings, using launchers like Projectivy or FLauncher, or keeping the TV offline with a streaming stick plugged in all reduce the clutter.The bigger reason behind the trend is fatigue. As tech analyst Carmi Levy puts it, people are "starting to get fed up" with devices that collect data at every turn.
Article Summary: Claude Code is being used to strip Android TV and Google TV sets back to the apps and HDMI inputs they paid for. Some users have bricked their sets, others have got stuck halfway, and security experts warn that cutting a connected TV off from updates could open the door to bigger problems. The bigger reason behind the trend is fatigue.

Article Title: Two sons of doctors built Vera Health, a free medical AI tool; a year after reaching just a few thousand users, their 12-person startup says it serves 800,000 clinicians in 190 countries and has raise
Article Text:
How it works

Built for their fathers

How Vera Health differs from general AI tools

A year ago, Vera Health had a few thousand users. The company says it now serves more than 800,000 clinicians in 190 countries, and it has raised a $28.5 million Series A to keep growing. Threshold Ventures led the round, with participation from Mantis VC and SV Angel. Existing investors Y Combinator and Gradient also put in more money, bringing Vera’s total funding to $32 million. The company says it has done this with only 12 employees and little marketing. Most clinicians found the tool through colleagues, it says. Vera also says it has been the most downloaded clinical app in the world every month since June, and that in September it was downloaded more often than OpenEvidence and Doximity combined. Those figures come from Appark data cited by the company. Monthly downloads have more than tripled since February.Vera is strongest in Europe, according to company data. About one in four physicians in Spain and Italy use it, as do about one in seven in France. The company says daily active users already exceed the monthly active users it had when it raised the round, and that clinicians now ask it hundreds of thousands of questions a day.Vera is a clinical search engine. Its pitch is that it finds the evidence first and writes the answer afterward. It searches more than 60 million peer-reviewed papers, guidelines, consensus statements and drug labels. It ranks sources by study design, level of evidence, cohort size, recency, journal quality and citation impact. Each claim links to its source and is color-coded by the strength of the evidence behind it. For a rare condition with only a small case series, the answer shows up red, so doctors can see how little supports it.“Unlike other tools, we believe there’s value in making uncertainty visible,” co-founder Maxime Allouch said.The tool is free for licensed clinicians and trainees. The company says it does not train on their questions and is HIPAA and GDPR compliant and SOC 2 Type II certified. It has a partnership with the American College of Emergency Physicians, which puts the group’s clinical policies into answers with source attribution. Health systems can also load their own protocols through a feature called Vera Spaces.Allouch and Taieb Bennani, both MIT graduates and sons of physicians, founded Vera in 2024 at Y Combinator. They first built it for their own fathers. “Everyone on our team is a clinician, or the child or sibling of one,” Bennani said. He credited that background for the product’s spread among doctors.The company says the new money will go toward its evidence infrastructure, expansion into more markets, and partnerships with medical societies, publishers and health systems. Bennani said the mission is to “close the gap between what medicine knows and what every patient receives,” and that he wants the gap measured in seconds rather than years.Unlike general-purpose chatbots, Vera Health is built specifically for medical professionals and emphasises evidence-based responses. The platform searches more than 60 million peer-reviewed publications, clinical guidelines, consensus statements and drug labels before generating answers. Each claim is linked to supporting research and includes indications of the strength of the available evidence."Clinicians are the best data scientists I've ever met," said Taieb Bennani, co-founder of Vera Health. He added that many members of the company are either clinicians themselves or family members of healthcare professionals, helping shape the product around real-world clinical needs.Meanwhile, co-founder Maxime Allouch said the platform is designed to make uncertainty visible rather than presenting every response with equal confidence, a key distinction in medical decision-making.
Article Summary: Vera Health has raised a $28.5 million Series A to keep growing. Its pitch is that it finds the evidence first and writes the answer afterward. It searches more than 60 million peer-reviewed papers, guidelines, consensus statements and drug labels.

Article Title: Oracle expands Nvidia AI chip deal, adds Google and other suppliers
Article Text:
Oracle expands Nvidia AI chip deal, adds Google and other suppliers

Oracle has expanded its cloud AI chip deal with Jensen Huang-led Nvidia while adding AI chips from other suppliers, including Google and Cerebras Systems, as it seeks to offer customers more options for running artificial intelligence workloads. Oracle and Nvidia said the cloud company would expand its use of Nvidia’s latest-generation Vera Rubin AI servers to "multi-gigawatt scale". “The expanded collaboration gives customers infrastructure for both the GPU-intensive work of training and serving frontier models and the CPU-intensive tasks agents perform between model calls, including executing tools, testing code and retrieving data. Customers can scale CPU and GPU resources independently to match their workloads, helping reduce idle capacity and put more of their infrastructure to productive use,” the company said in an announcement.Oracle is also changing parts of its AI infrastructure. It plans to use its own Acceleron networking chips in some Nvidia-based systems instead of certain Nvidia networking chips. The company will also begin offering Google’s tensor processing unit (TPU) chips for the first time."Different AI workloads have different compute needs," Mahesh Thiagarajan, president of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, said in a statement."That choice gives (customers) the flexibility to choose the right infrastructure for the performance, throughput and economics of each AI workload.”Beyond Google, Oracle plans to offer chips from SambaNova Systems and Cerebras Systems. Both companies make chips designed for AI inference, the process in which an AI system responds to user requests.While Nvidia leads the market for chips used to train AI systems, the inference market has a wider range of competitors. "That's a massive expansion of our customer base of tier-one customers," Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman said of the Oracle deal in an interview with Reuters. "We're being deployed in other people's data centers at large scale."
Article Summary: Oracle expands its cloud AI chip deal with Jensen Huang-led Nvidia. The company will also begin offering Google’s tensor processing unit (TPU) chips for the first time. Oracle plans to offer chips from SambaNova Systems and Cerebras Systems.

Article Title: Google DeepMind launches Genie 4, CEO Sundar Pichai calls it ‘our most realistic and interactive world model’
Article Text:
Excited to share Genie 4 today our most realistic and interactive world model:

- steer dynamic environments in real time, shaping events, camera angles, and actions

- generate native audio matched to the world, from realistic background sounds to characters who can converse in real time!

- simulate photorealistic scenes and real-world physics

- create more coherent multi-step events through reasoning from Gemini

We've started to roll out as a research preview to trusted testers.

Coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners via the Gemini API and AI Studio.

Genie 4 is built on Gemini Intelligence

Google lists four core breakthroughs in Genie 4

Real-time scene direction

Advanced physics and motion

Native audio generation

Complex multi-step simulation

Google DeepMind has officially unveiled Genie 4, its world artificial intelligence (AI) model that introduces real-time, interactive world simulation with native audio and realism. The system allows users to generate and actively navigate dynamic environments, steering scenes on the fly while the model simultaneously calculates physics, character behavior, and soundscapes. Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted the milestone, calling Genie 4 “our most realistic and interactive world model.”Genie 4 is not a standalone graphics engine; it directly integrates the multimodal reasoning capabilities of Google’s Gemini family:Gemini Omni: Anchors each simulation in authentic real-world appearances, physical dynamics and visual continuity.Gemini reasoning models: Maintain scene logic, ensuring events unfold with cause-and-effect coherence over time.Gemini 3.8 Flash: Operates as an active agent in the loop. As Genie 4 renders the world, Gemini 3.8 Flash tracks incoming frames, breaks broad goals into sequential steps, verifies that actions succeed, and adapts plans instantly whenever the scene shifts or a user intervenes.Google DeepMind detailed four primary technical advancements that define the new world model:Users can explore simulated environments using standard keyboard controls for navigation and camera positioning, while using plain text prompts to alter the world in real time. They can change the weather, adjust camera angles, or introduce new characters and objects.Google says that Genie 4 delivers a significant leap in physical accuracy, accurately rendering complex interactions such as aerodynamics, collisions, and environmental resistance. Character animation sees an equally sharp upgrade: digital figures move naturally, interact organically with their surroundings, and respond immediately to real-time steering.As the first real-time world model to generate synchronised audio natively, Genie 4 produces sound directly alongside visual frames, Google says. This includes contextual ambient soundscapes, such as wind through trees or breaking ocean waves as well as background music.Crucially, the model handles interactive, real-time spoken dialogue. Characters converse, react, and respond on the fly to user prompts and unfolding environmental events.By pairing world generation with advanced AI reasoning, Genie 4 can simulate multi-stage events, allowing developers to see how artificial agents navigate complex settings before deploying them into real-world scenarios.
Article Summary: Google DeepMind unveils Genie 4, its world artificial intelligence (AI) model. System introduces real-time, interactive world simulation with native audio and realism. System allows users to generate and actively navigate dynamic environments, steering scenes on the fly. Model simultaneously calculates physics, character behavior, and soundscapes.

Article Title: Scale AI’s Outlier has more than 900,000 freelancers; a privacy group alleges up to 19 trackers monitor workers and is asking European regulators to fine the company
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

What do the complaints allege about worker tracking

“You don't work when you want,

“You work when the platform wants you to and there are tasks available.”

Why are Scale AI’s identity checks being challenged

Scale AI’s Outlier faces complaints over alleged monitoring of freelancers. According to a report by the news agency Reuters, European digital privacy advocacy group noyb has filed five complaints in France, Italy, the Netherlands and Austria against the company founded by Meta’s current chief AI officer and highest-paid employee, Alexandr Wang. The complaints allege that the platform illegally tracks people who produce training data for artificial intelligence (AI)models. According to the Reuters report, the complaints say up to 19 trackers monitor workers, including by recording keystrokes and mouse movements every few seconds.Outlier has more than 900,000 freelancers performing tasks for clients such as Meta, OpenAI and Google. Noyb is asking European regulators to fine Scale AI and examine how the platform assigns work. The complaints also challenge its identity checks and how it handles workers’ requests for their personal data.The complaints, which Reuters reviewed, describe monitoring that records workers’ activity throughout their tasks. An investigation by Paris-based research collective DiPLab found that the resulting data file could be reconstructed into a video replaying a work session from beginning to end.Thomas Le Bonniec, who spent two years studying Outlier for DiPLab, also questioned how much control freelancers have over their schedules.” Le Bonniec said.Noyb’s request that regulators examine task allocation raises concerns about how the platform decides which work is available to freelancers.Workers must submit identification documents and a facial video to Persona, an identity verification company. The complaints allege that these checks were invasive, repeated without explanation, and breached European Union rules governing biometric data, which can identify people through physical characteristics. However, these are mere allegations in the complaints, not findings announced by regulators.DiPLab’s investigation also identified game-like mechanisms that encouraged workers to complete tasks, with bonuses as a key part of the incentive system. Citing worker interviews, Le Bonniec said Outlier offered bonuses of $100 to $200 for completing 200 tasks within 24 hours.He pointed to a 2021 fine Italy’s data protection authority imposed on delivery platform Glovo for similar gamification practices, in which rewards or targets are used to influence workers’ behaviour.Separately, four workers requested copies of their personal data from Outlier between December 2025 and May 2026. According to the complaints, none received an answer.
Article Summary: Scale AI’s Outlier faces complaints over alleged monitoring of freelancers. European digital privacy advocacy group noyb has filed five complaints against the company. The complaints allege that the platform illegally tracks people who produce training data for artificial intelligence (AI)models.
